text:
Defending champions are supposed to coast through November. The Hurricanes are 15-3-2, first in the league with 32 points, and they've played like a team that forgot it already won. Thursday in Helsinki was the postcard: Sebastian Aho scored twice in front of a Finnish crowd, Taylor Hall played his 1,000th game, and Carolina beat Seattle 4-1 for its third straight win.

The record isn't luck. Carolina takes 58% of the expected goals at five on five (expected goals measure the quality of chances) and allows just 2.59 per 60, and it has outscored teams 82-45. Our race simulations give the Canes essentially a certain playoff spot and an 80% chance at the Metropolitan. The line of Nikolaj Ehlers, Logan Stankoven and Jackson Blake has outscored teams 12-1 together, and the Aho line with William Carrier and Andrei Svechnikov is 12-6.

If there's anything to watch, it's how much of the scoring is running ahead of the chances. Stankoven has 14 points in his last 10 on 6.9 expected, a pace that cools for almost everyone. Pyotr Kochetkov, meanwhile, has been better than his save rate looks over his last five starts. A champion whose goalie is underrated is not a problem we'd want to solve.
